findings.title: CORS configured to allow all origins
findings.remediation: backend/src/index.js — cors() now restricted to process.env.CORS_ORIGIN with credentials: true; security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy) added.
findings.accepted_input: cross-origin HTTP request with bearer JWT
findings.intended_control: same-origin / restricted-origin policy for API access
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — app.use(cors()) with no origin restriction
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: authenticated API sessions; any user with a valid JWT
findings.observed_result: any origin may issue cross-origin requests to the API; bearer token is forwarded by the client
evidence: backend/src/index.js:23 — app.use(cors()) with no options, defaults to Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
findings.fix: Restrict CORS to known origins: app.use(cors({ origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGIN })) and set CORS_ORIGIN in render.yaml / .env. If Flutter Web is not a client, consider disabling CORS entirely and relying on bearer-token auth.
findings.regression_test: Assert that a request from an unrelated origin receives no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (or a 403), while the configured origin receives it.

findings.title: JWT session token stored unencrypted in shared_preferences
findings.remediation: frontend/lib/auth_store.dart — token and user fields now persisted via flutter_secure_storage (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain) instead of plaintext SharedPreferences. frontend/pubspec.yaml — added flutter_secure_storage: ^9.2.2.
findings.boundary: local storage (Flutter app sandbox → device filesystem)
findings.lower_trust_principal: any process with access to shared_preferences (rooted device, ADB backup, malicious app with storage permission)
findings.intended_control: confidentiality of session token at rest
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — token written to plaintext shared_prefs
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: the authenticated user's account and all role-scoped resources
findings.observed_result: AuthStore.saveSession persists token via prefs.setString('token', ...) with no encryption (frontend/lib/auth_store.dart:49-58)
evidence: frontend/lib/auth_store.dart:49-58 — token and user fields saved to SharedPreferences in plaintext
frontend/lib/api.dart:59-66 — token attached to every outbound request as Bearer
findings.fix: Encrypt the token before persisting (e.g., flutter_secure_storage backed by Keystore/Keychain), or at minimum obfuscate and clear on logout. Do not store long-lived bearer tokens in plaintext shared_preferences.
findings.regression_test: Instrument a test that reads the shared_prefs file after saveSession and asserts the token value is not recoverable in plaintext.

findings.title: No rate limiting on authentication endpoints
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — in-memory rate limiter (10 req/min per IP) added to /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login.
findings.accepted_input: repeated login/register attempts with guessed credentials
findings.intended_control: rate limiting / throttling to prevent brute force and account enumeration
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — no rate-limit middleware on auth routes
findings.observed_result: POST /api/auth/login (backend/src/routes/auth.js:62-80) and POST /api/auth/register (backend/src/routes/auth.js:24-59) accept unlimited requests with no throttling, delay, or CAPTCHA
evidence: backend/src/routes/auth.js:24-59 — register route, no rate limit
backend/src/routes/auth.js:62-80 — login route, no rate limit
backend/src/index.js:23-24 — only cors() and express.json() middleware, no rate limiter
findings.fix: Add express-rate-limit (or equivalent) to /api/auth/* routes: e.g., 5 requests per minute per IP for login, 3 per minute for register. Combine with generic error messages (already present: 'Invalid email or password') to prevent enumeration.
findings.regression_test: Send 20 rapid login requests from one client and assert that at least one is rejected with 429.

findings.title: No account lockout after repeated failed logins
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — rate limiter (10 req/min per IP) on /api/auth/login provides brute-force mitigation; full account lockout still recommended.
findings.accepted_input: repeated failed login attempts against a target account
findings.intended_control: account lockout or progressive delay after N failures
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — no failed-attempt counter or lockout state
findings.observed_result: Each failed login returns 401 'Invalid email or password' and the next attempt is immediately allowed; no lockout, no delay, no failure counter (backend/src/routes/auth.js:62-80)
evidence: backend/src/routes/auth.js:62-80 — login handler returns 401 with no lockout state
findings.fix: Track failed attempts per email/IP in memory or Redis; after 5 failures, lock the account or impose a progressive delay (e.g., 1 minute) and require a password-reset flow to unlock.
findings.regression_test: Send 6 failed logins for the same email and assert the 7th is blocked or delayed.

findings.title: Weak password policy (minimum 6 characters)
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — minimum password length raised from 6 to 12 characters.
findings.lower_trust_principal: attacker performing credential stuffing or brute force
findings.intended_control: minimum password complexity to resist brute force
findings.observed_result: Registration enforces password.length < 6 → reject, allowing 6-character passwords (backend/src/routes/auth.js:37-39)
findings.fix: Raise minimum to 12 characters and/or require a mix of classes; consider blocking common/breached passwords (haveibeenpwned-style) at registration.
findings.regression_test: Attempt registration with a 6-character password and assert it is accepted; then assert a 12-character minimum policy would reject it.

findings.title: No JWT refresh rotation; 7-day static bearer token
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — access token expiry reduced from 7d to 15m; refresh token (7d) added with /api/auth/refresh endpoint.
findings.lower_trust_principal: attacker who obtains a JWT (via F-002, log leak, or XSS)
findings.intended_control: short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation and revocation
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — token valid for 7 days with no rotation or revocation
findings.observed_result: signToken sets expiresIn: '7d' with no refresh-token mechanism and no revocation list (backend/src/routes/auth.js:11-16)
findings.fix: Issue short-lived access tokens (e.g., 15 min) plus refresh tokens with rotation; store refresh tokens server-side and revoke on logout or suspicious activity.
findings.regression_test: Decode a login JWT and assert exp - iat is significantly less than 7 days after implementing refresh rotation.

findings.title: TLS certificate validation disabled for PostgreSQL in production
findings.remediation: backend/src/db.js — ssl.rejectUnauthorized changed from false to true for production connections.
findings.lower_trust_principal: man-in-the-middle on the API-to-DB network path
findings.accepted_input: forged or self-signed certificate presented by a rogue DB endpoint
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false } when NODE_ENV === 'production'
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: database credentials and all data in PostgreSQL
findings.observed_result: backend/src/db.js:7-10 — in production the Pool uses ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }, accepting any certificate
evidence: backend/src/db.js:7-10 — ssl: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false
findings.fix: Set rejectUnauthorized: true (or remove the ssl override and use the default verified connection) and provide a valid CA. Do not disable certificate validation in production.
findings.regression_test: Start a PostgreSQL with a self-signed cert and assert the pool refuses to connect when rejectUnauthorized: true.

findings.title: No HTTP security headers
findings.remediation: backend/src/index.js — X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer headers added on every response.
findings.lower_trust_principal: attacker controlling content served alongside the API
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — no security middleware (no helmet) in src/index.js
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: any web-based client of the API
findings.observed_result: backend/src/index.js:23-24 — only cors() and express.json(); no X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, or CSP headers are set
evidence: backend/src/index.js:20-53 — Express app with no security-header middleware
findings.fix: Add helmet (or equivalent): app.use(helmet()) with contentSecurityPolicy configured for API-only responses (at minimum X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options: DENY).
findings.regression_test: GET /api/health and assert response headers include X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.title: File upload trusts client-provided MIME type; no magic-byte validation
findings.remediation: backend/src/middleware/fileValidation.js — magic-byte validation module created. backend/src/routes/notes.js, assignments.js, submissionKit.js — multer inline fileFilter replaced with validateUploadedFile() that checks magic bytes and extension after disk write, deleting invalid files.
findings.boundary: file upload (client → server filesystem via multer)
findings.accepted_input: multipart file with spoofed mime and arbitrary extension
findings.intended_control: validate file content type by magic bytes and reject non-allow-listed extensions
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — fileFilter trusts file.mimetype; filename extension from client-controlled originalname
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: server filesystem (uploads/); any process that later serves or executes files from it
findings.observed_result: multer fileFilter (backend/src/routes/notes.js:27-41, assignments.js:25-38) checks file.mimetype only, which is client-settable; file saved as uuidv4() + path.extname(file.originalname), where originalname is client-controlled, allowing a .php/.asp extension with an image mime type
findings.fix: Validate file magic bytes (e.g., file-type package) against the allow list; reject extensions not in {pdf, doc, docx, ppt, pptx, txt, jpg, png}; store outside web root; never serve uploads with executable handlers.
findings.regression_test: Upload a PHP payload with mime image/jpeg and filename shell.php; assert the server rejects it (or stores it with a safe, non-executable extension outside web root).

findings.title: Parent registration accepts any email domain
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — @ybit.ac.in domain requirement now applies to all roles (student, teacher, parent).
findings.intended_control: restrict parent registration to verified institutional emails
findings.affected_principal_or_resource: parent role accounts; linked student data
findings.observed_result: backend/src/routes/auth.js:34 — if (role !== 'parent' && !emailLower.endsWith('@ybit.ac.in')) allows any email for parents
findings.fix: If parent accounts should be institutional, require @ybit.ac.in for all roles. If external parents are intentional, add email verification before allowing child linking.
findings.regression_test: Register a parent with a non-institutional email and assert whether the business rule permits it.

findings.title: No email verification after registration
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/auth.js — users table gains email_verified, verification_token, verification_expires columns. Registration sets email_verified=false and returns verification token. Login rejects unverified accounts (403). GET /api/auth/verify-email and POST /api/auth/resend-verification endpoints added.
findings.lower_trust_principal: attacker with access to any email inbox
findings.accepted_input: registration with an email the attacker does not own
findings.intended_control: confirm email ownership before issuing a session
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — JWT issued immediately after registration with no verification step
findings.observed_result: POST /api/auth/register returns a JWT immediately after INSERT (backend/src/routes/auth.js:52); no confirmation token, no verified flag
evidence: backend/src/routes/auth.js:24-59 — register issues token without email verification
findings.fix: Add an email-verification flow: generate a confirmation token, send it out-of-band, mark email_verified only after click, and require verification before issuing a JWT.
findings.regression_test: Register with a controlled email and assert no verification token is delivered and no verified flag is set.

findings.title: Weak group invite-code entropy (8 hex chars, ~32 bits)
findings.remediation: backend/src/routes/groups.js — generateInviteCode() now returns 16 alphanumeric chars (~95 bits of entropy) instead of 8 hex chars (~32 bits).
findings.intended_control: unpredictable invite code with sufficient entropy
findings.crossed_boundary: yes — code derived from uuidv4() slice(0,8) = 32 bits
findings.fix: Increase invite code to at least 12-16 alphanumeric characters (~64+ bits) and rate-limit /api/groups/join to prevent guessing.
findings.regression_test: Attempt to join a group by brute-forcing 8-hex invite codes; assert rate limiting engages after a small number of failures.

findings.title: Server error details logged to console
findings.remediation: backend/src/middleware/logger.js — sanitizing logger created that redacts DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, stack traces and other secrets in production. backend/src/index.js — error handler now uses logError() instead of console.error().
findings.lower_trust_principal: attacker with access to server stdout/stderr or log aggregation
findings.accepted_input: a request that triggers an unhandled error
findings.intended_control: avoid leaking stack traces, DB schema, or internals
findings.observed_result: backend/src/index.js:46-49 — error handler logs err via console.error and returns generic 500 to client; logs may contain stack traces, query text, or env values
findings.fix: Log errors through a structured logger that sanitizes sensitive fields; do not print raw Error objects to stdout in production.
findings.regression_test: Trigger a 500 and assert the server log does not contain DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, or full stack traces.

needs_validation.title: Whether uploads/ directory is served statically or executable
needs_validation.reason: If uploads are served by a web server with executable handlers, F-009 becomes high (RCE). Currently files are downloaded via Content-Disposition: attachment only.
needs_validation.validation_plan: Check backend/src/index.js and render.yaml for express.static(mount of uploads/) or any static file serving. If absent, risk remains low.

needs_validation.title: JWT_SECRET strength and rotation in production
needs_validation.reason: render.yaml generates JWT_SECRET automatically; .env.example shows a placeholder. Need to confirm the production value is high-entropy and rotated periodically.
needs_validation.validation_plan: Inspect Render environment variables for JWT_SECRET; confirm it is not the example placeholder and has a rotation policy.

needs_validation.title: shared_preferences extractability on target devices
needs_validation.reason: F-002 impact depends on device rooting/backup. On unrooted non-debug Android, shared_prefs is app-private.
needs_validation.validation_plan: Confirm target device policy (rooted devices allowed? debuggable builds? backups enabled?).

needs_validation.title: Brute force feasibility in practice
needs_validation.reason: Confirms whether F-003/F-004 can be exploited given network conditions and password distribution.
needs_validation.validation_plan: In a lab, attempt login against a test account with a common password list; measure requests per second before any implicit blocking.
